about: Runs in which the WebAssembly assembler does not reproduce the official EDIT68K.exe v5.16.1 (see known-differences.ts). Each entry is a finding for the owner it names. The official result is in golden/<id>/<label>.L68. "ours" is what the port produces today for each run (error and warning count, SHA-256 of the canonical .L68 and .S68): the test fails when the port produces anything else, and its message gives the new values.

differences.reason: An `IFNE FWD` block with `S SET 5`, `DC.B S` and a MACRO, where FWD is defined further down: the official assembler gives `DC.B S` = 05, no error, and lists FWD, M and S in its symbol table. The port reports `Undefined symbol` for the DC.B line and emits 00 (1 error instead of 0; only FWD in the symbol table). In pass 1 eval pushes an unwritten local for the undefined FWD (EVAL.CPP:76): the port starts it at 0 (P7), so the block is skipped in pass 1 and in pass 2 define() finds no S (the case P14 guards); the original's value was not 0, so it assembled the block in pass 1 too. The native build of the unpatched sources reproduces the official listing.
differences.owner: engine/asm (PATCHES.md P7 at EVAL.CPP:76, assembler §9.3.3; P14, §9.3.9)

differences.reason: A macro body line with a valid printf conversion (`DC.B '%d%s%%'`): in the official assembler the expansion ends at that line, with Macros Expanded on and off - neither the line nor the ENDM line reaches the listing, no code is emitted for it (with the option off the next statement's address shows it: 1004 against the port's 100A) and no error is reported. The port expands the line literally (6 bytes of object code more). The original copies each macro body line into its macro store with fprintf(tmpFile, line) (MACRO.CPP:106, assembler §9.3.4), so the line is a format string and its result depends on what the conversions read from the stack; this is what the binary did under Wine, in this program. The port copies the line literally (P5).

`ENDI` with nothing open, followed by an `IF` without THEN: the official assembler reports `Undefined symbol` for the ENDI and lists a generated label line (`_020C002A`, a value read from an empty stack), and then assembles the IF with a correct branch (`6600 0008`) and only the `THEN expected` warning. The port reports `Invalid syntax` for the ENDI and an additional `Undefined symbol` with `BNE _00000000` for the IF (6 errors instead of 5, and every later address is 4 lower).
differences.owner: engine/asm (assembler §9.3.6: terminator with an empty stack)
